question.text: The density of a liquid contained in a tank of area <math><mn>0.5</mn><mi> </mi><msup><mrow><mn>m</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1200</mn><mn> k</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mn>m</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The container is closed by a massless, frictionless and movable piston and there is a hole of area <math><mn>1</mn><mi> </mi><mn>c</mn><msup><mrow><mn>m</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> near the bottom of the container. A load of <math><mn>30</mn><mi> </mi><mn>k</mn><mn>g</mn></math> is placed on the piston and the height of liquid level is <math><mn>75</mn><mi> </mi><mn>c</mn><mn>m</mn></math> above the bottom. What is the initial flow velocity (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>) of the liquid? [Take, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mn>s</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>]

solution.text:
Let the velocity of efflux at point 2 is v.



Given, a=1 cm2, A=0.5 m2=0.5×104 cm2

Applying continuity equation,

AV=av

V=aAv

Since, a≪A,V≪v,  V2 is negligible.

Pressure at (1),

p1=p0+mgA

=p0+30×100.5

=p0+600

Pressure at (2) ,

p2=p0

where, p0 is atmospheric pressure.

Applying Bernoulli's equation between (1) and (2),

p1+ρgh+12ρV2=ρ2+12ρv2

V2 is negligible, then

p0+600+1200×10×0.75

=p0+12×1200v2

600v2=9600

⇒ v2=16

⇒ v=4 m s-1
